Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle Belarusian сокъ (sok), from Old East Slavic сокъ (sokŭ), from Proto-Slavic *sokъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sakás, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷós.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sok]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

сок • (sok) m inan (genitive со́ку, nominative plural со́кі, genitive plural со́каў)

  1. juice

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
сок
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *sokъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sakás, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷós.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sɔk]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔk

Noun

[edit]

сок • (sok) m

  1. juice
  2. sap (the juice of plants)

[edit]

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian сок (sok).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsok/, [ˈso̞k]
  • Hyphenation: сок

Noun

[edit]

сок • (sok)

  1. juice

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sokъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sakás, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷós.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sɔk]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔk

Noun

[edit]

сок • (sok) m (relational adjective сочен, diminutive сокче)

  1. juice
  2. sap (juice of plants)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of сок
singular plural
indefinite сок (sok) сокови (sokovi)
definite unspecified сокот (sokot) соковите (sokovite)
definite proximal соков (sokov) соковиве (sokovive)
definite distal сокон (sokon) соковине (sokovine)
vocative соку (soku) сокови (sokovi)
count form — сока (soka)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • соковник (sokovnik)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak sok, from Proto-Slavic *sokъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sakás, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷós. Usage and retention vis-à-vis Slovak šťava probably influenced by Carpathian Rusyn сок (sok) and later Serbo-Croatian сок / sok.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsɔk]
  • Rhymes: -ɔk
  • Hyphenation: сок

Noun

[edit]

сок (sok) m inan (relational adjective сочни)

  1. juice
    Synonym: (less common) юшка (juška)
    овоцни сок ― ovocni sok ― fruit juice
  2. sap

Declension

[edit]
Declension of сок (sok)
singular plural
nominative сок (sok) соки (soki)
genitive соку (soku) сокох (sokox)
dative соку (soku) соком (sokom)
accusative сок (sok) соки (soki)
instrumental соком (sokom) соками (sokami)
locative соку (soku) сокох (sokox)
vocative соку (soku) соки (soki)

Related terms

[edit]
adjectives
  • соковити (sokoviti)

[edit]
  • Medʹeši, H.; Fejsa, M.; Timko-Djitko, O. (2010), “сок”, in Ramač, Ju., editor, Руско-сербски словнїк [Rusyn-Serbian Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “juice”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 31

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • сокъ (sok) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

From Old East Slavic сокъ (sokŭ), from Proto-Slavic *sȍkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sakás, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷós.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sok]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ok

Noun

[edit]

сок • (sok) m inan (genitive со́ка, nominative plural со́ки, genitive plural со́ков)

  1. juice
  2. sap
  3. (figuratively or poetic) This term needs a translation to English. Please help out and add a translation, then remove the text {{rfdef}}. an outstanding part of something
  4. (vulgar, slang) cum, semen
